gaps.sentence: We see our grandparents ___ other weekend.
gaps.explanation: 'Every other weekend' means alternate weekends; 'each other' has a different, reciprocal meaning.

gaps.sentence: Not ___ candidates applied for the position.
gaps.explanation: 'Not many' is used with countable plurals like candidates; 'not much' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: She has two children. One lives in Leeds, and ___ lives in York.
gaps.hint: one of a pair of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... the other ...' is the pattern for exactly two; 'another' would imply more than two.

gaps.sentence: ___ of her two brothers lives abroad.
gaps.explanation: 'Each of her two brothers lives ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' and 'both/all' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: ___ single room in the hotel was fully booked.
gaps.explanation: 'Every single room' is the emphatic collocation meaning 'without exception'.

gaps.sentence: There are trees on ___ side of the road.
gaps.hint: singular noun: each of the two sides
gaps.explanation: 'Either side' means each of the two sides; 'both' would need the plural 'sides'.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: This is ___ beautiful beach on the island.
gaps.explanation: 'The most beautiful' is the superlative form used for comparisons within a group.
